One-time pad.why: Vernam's 1917 cipher, a classic named system; Vernam and OTP are valid aliases.

Affine cipher.why: Named classical monoalphabetic cipher; 'affine' is a short form of the same name, not a generic word.

Book cipher.why: Named classical cipher using a shared book; 'book code' is a loose alias that can be confused with codebooks.

Nihilist cipher.why: Real 19th-century Russian revolutionary cipher, but known mainly to crypto-history specialists, so it sits closer to race than NPE.

Hill cipher.why: Real 1929 polygraphic cipher. The alias 'Hill' is a common English word and should be dropped as too generic.

Purple cipher.why: Real WWII Japanese diplomatic cipher machine; 'Angooki Taipu B' is its actual Japanese designation.

Pigpen cipher.why: Real symbol substitution cipher; 'pigpen' drops only the word 'cipher', so it is an alias of the same entry.

ADFGX.why: Real WWI German field cipher; specialist knowledge fits race.

Hebern machine.why: Real 1920s rotor machine, but its name is mostly known to crypto historians, so race fits better than NPE.

Columnar transposition.why: Real classical transposition cipher, widely taught in intro crypto; memory leak is too deep for it, NPE fits.

Bazeries cylinder.why: Real 1891 cylinder cipher device; it is specialist knowledge, so race fits better than NPE.

Cardan grille.why: Real 16th-century grille cipher; 'Cardano grille' is a real spelling of the same name, and 'grille cipher' is a broad but acceptable alias.

Lorenz cipher.why: Real WWII German teleprinter cipher; 'Tunny' is the real British codename, and NPE fits.

Baconian cipher.why: Real 1605 cipher by Francis Bacon, widely known in puzzles and classical crypto texts.

Jefferson wheel cipher.why: Real device described in Jefferson's papers, but specialist-only, so race fits better than NPE.

Running key cipher.why: Named classical method using a book text as key; common in intro crypto. 'running key' drops only 'cipher', so it is an alias.

Gronsfeld cipher.why: Real numeric-key Vigenère variant; specialist-level, so race fits and heisenbug is too deep.

Playfair cipher.why: Real 1854 digraph cipher, widely taught in crypto courses; NPE fits better than memory leak.

Enigma.why: Real and the most iconic historical cipher machine, so most people name it first. Off-by-one fits better than NPE.

Four-square cipher.why: Real 1902 Delastelle cipher; 'foursquare' is the same name without the hyphen, so it is an alias. Race fits.
